_README: Scope decisions for the Salon de la Photo migration. Each rule is a DECISION taken once and applied to every page (doctrine: decisions printed into the workflow, never re-litigated per page). Every selector was verified against the captured corpus (27 pages) before being listed; the counts in each reason are measured, not estimated. scope_apply.py rebuilds the scoped mirror from local-mirror-prescope on every run, so rules never compound.
_keptEmbeds_README: Third-party frames the source genuinely uses as CONTENT, each a modelling decision rather than junk: YouTube (home video band), Weezevent (2 ticketing widgets on lien-billetterie), Google My Maps (photo-pass venue map), impactco2 (transport calculator on dates-acces-horaires). cdn.jsdelivr.net is not an embed but the swiffy-slider stylesheet the partners carousel depends on — localize_site left it as external residue; step_assets must vendor it into static/ so the migrated site has no CDN dependency. Everything NOT listed here must be scope-excluded (probes/mirror-selfcontained.py enforces it).

rules.reason: OneTrust cookie banner + preference centre, present on 27/27 captured pages. Not site content: Jahia ships its own consent module. Left in, it dominates the zoning map (it produced 20+ of the 35 ABSOLUTE keys: Ot Grp Hdr1, Ot Sdk Row, Ot Pc Scrollbar, Dialog, Ot Chkbox) and would be migrated as chrome. The SDK LOADER is a separate inline script pointing at cdn.cookielaw.org (27/27 pages): removing only the banner DOM left the mirror still fetching OneTrust at review time — caught by probes/mirror-selfcontained.py's inline-loader scan, not by the DOM rule.

Zero-height SXA plain-html spacer, exactly 27 instances (one per page), no text, no iframe, no script. Layout plumbing, nothing to contribute. The plain-html instances that DO carry an iframe (5: YouTube, impactco2 transport, Google Maps, 2x Weezevent ticketing) are deliberately NOT matched — they are real embeds and each is a modelling decision.

match.selector: script[data-cf-beacon], script[chatbotid], link[href*='chatbase'], div[id^='chatbase'], button[aria-controls='chatbase-bubble-window'], iframe[src*='googletagmanager'], script[src*='googletagmanager'], script:-soup-contains('googletagmanager'), script:-soup-contains('gtag('), script[src*='dobby.weezevent'], script[src*='weezevent.net']

rules.reason: Runtime telemetry and third-party widgets, not site content. Cloudflare's own RUM beacon (script[data-cf-beacon]) and the chatbase chatbot survived localization with rewritten relative srcs, so reviewing the mirror produced POST /cdn-cgi/rum -> 404 and GET /api/get-chatbot-styles -> 404 plus a live chat bubble over the hero (operator observation 2026-08-03, read as a Cloudflare block). The GTM noscript iframe is a 0x0 hidden tracker. None of it is migratable content: Jahia has its own analytics/consent story, and a chatbot is a post-migration integration decision. The GTM bootstrap is an INLINE script that builds its own src at runtime, so an attribute-URL selector misses it — matched by text instead (soupsieve :-soup-contains). The entity DETAIL pages carry a further tracker the menu pages did not: dobby.weezevent.net/<uuid>.js on 131 of 159 pages (Weezevent's remarketing beacon, distinct from the widget.weezevent.com ticketing iframe which IS kept content). Only surfaced once the corpus included detail pages — a menu-only capture cannot see it.

SXA structured-data components (3 instances) hold nothing but a JSON-LD <script>: zero visible text. SEO metadata belongs on the Jahia side to the sdpmix:seo mixin, not to a migrated content component.

pagesToCrawl.reason: 3 audience landing pages (amateur-averti, createur-contenus, professionnel) reached from the profil-visiteur card grid. Not dated, not card-reached prose -> PAGES per the tie-break rule. Crawl as children of salon/profil-visiteur.

A THIRD ticketing URL beyond the menu's lien-billetterie and billet, linked from the home hero slide ('Acheter mon billet') and from dates-acces-horaires. The site's primary CTA cannot resolve to nothing: crawl it as a page.
The exhibitor-facing area ('Devenir exposant', linked from the top bar and the FAQ). Crawl the landing page; its sub-tree (exposants/salon/rse/...) follows the same decision.
Press/creator accreditation, linked from the FAQ and the ticketing page. Crawl as a page; if it turns out to be a pure form, it becomes an accepted external target instead.

The catalogue's three AXIS LISTING pages — /catalogue/exhibitors, /catalogue/brands, /catalogue/products ('Voir tous les exposants / marques / produits', CatalogFilterBar-link). Each becomes a Jahia page carrying one sdp:jcrQuery over its matching contentFolder. The per-item details under /Exposant/, /Marque/ and /Produit/ are entities and are declared in the mainresource map instead.
LEGAL page, linked from the footer on all 27 pages and present in /sitemap.xml. A migrated site without its legal notice is not shippable.
GDPR / data-protection page, footer on all 27 pages, in the sitemap. Legally required.
RGAA accessibility statement, footer on all 27 pages, in the sitemap. Legally required in France for this kind of site.
Cookie policy, footer on all 27 pages. Not in the sitemap (OneTrust may serve it) — crawl it and confirm it is a real page; otherwise it becomes an accepted target.
HTML sitemap page, footer on all 27 pages, in the sitemap. In Jahia this can render from the page tree instead of holding frozen links — decide at build time.
An entire SECTION absent from the main menu: the press area landing, linked from the footer and from the actualite-photo pages. Its 7 press releases are declared as an entity folder.
A partner story page under the CSR section, published in /sitemap.xml and linked from salon_rse. One page, not an entity family (no date, no listing) -> crawl it as a child page of salon/rse.

acceptedTargets.reason: A client-side favourites feature (the 'mes favoris' tray on programme-salon and the catalogue), not a server page. No Jahia equivalent in scope: the feature is out of scope for the migration.
Sitecore's own 404 service endpoint (notfound.aspx), linked by a BROKEN anchor on salon_rse. A defect in the source, not content to migrate.
A PDF asset (Ecogestes-Visiteurs-Comexposium.pdf) served from the Sitecore media library. Imported into the Jahia DAM by the asset step, never a page.
The Sitecore site-search page. Its backend is the SXA search index, which does not exist in Jahia; the replacement is Jahia's own search module, configured post-migration. Not a page to migrate.

Two social-campaign landing pages (campagnes/zooms-facebook, campagnes/zooms-instagram) for the Prix du Public des Zooms, one per channel. Present in /sitemap.xml, linked from NO page on the site and reached only from social posts — they are tracking entry points, not site content. Out of scope; revisit if the campaign is being re-run on the Jahia site.

A BROKEN IMAGE ON THE SOURCE: 16 references on the 'Portrait de personnalite' programme pages point at /img/placeholder_profile_picture.08282499.jpg, which the origin answers with HTTP 404 (an HTML error page). Nothing to localize and nothing to migrate — the defect is upstream. Recorded so the self-containment gate stays honest rather than being widened.

A THIRD catalogue URL shape (/catalog-exhibitor-full/<exhibitor>), linked from programme event detail pages to the speaker's exhibiting company. Only visible once detail pages were captured. It belongs to the DEFERRED catalogue decision (sdp:directoryEntry, 33 details across /Exposant/, /Marque/, /Produit/): when that type is approved this becomes a fourth urlPrefix on the exhibitor folder rather than an accepted target.
A MALFORMED SOURCE LINK: the programme detail template leaked an unresolved placeholder into the href (`/programme-salon/,-w-,/,-w-,`), on 2 event pages. Broken upstream, nothing to migrate.

A LEGACY URL shape (capitalised /Le-salon/Actualites/<slug>) still linked from one article's prose; the live site 301s it to /actualite-photo/actus/<slug>. The write-time link rewire maps it onto the migrated article when the slug resolves; recorded here so the census does not demand a page for a redirect.

_targets_README: pagesToCrawl and acceptedTargets are the DECISION register for internal link targets the menu-scoped capture does not reach. probes/link-census.py fails on any internal link whose target is in none of: captured pages, mainresource urlPrefixes, the sitemap, pagesToCrawl, acceptedTargets. A decision may be 'crawl it' or 'accept it out of scope', but it may never be silence.
